a.text: Hidden inside あ is a curly little letter “a”. Find the a, say “ah!”

i.text: Two eels standing side by side: “ee-ee”.

u.text: The bottom stroke curves like a sideways U – “ooh”.

e.text: An exotic bird with a feather on its head: “eh?” – it looks surprised.

o.text: You can spot two little o’s in お. Unlike あ, it has no “a” inside.

ka.text: A mosquito with its wings out. In Japanese, mosquito is 蚊 – “ka”!

ki.text: き is a key with its teeth sticking out.

ku.text: The open beak of a cuckoo bird: “ku-ku”.

ke.text: Long wiggly strands of kelp swaying in the water.

ko.text: Two worms lying next to each other, co-habitating – “ko”.

sa.text: Two hands stirring a bowl of chunky salsa – “sa”.

shi.text: A shepherd’s hook catching a sheep – “shi”. Exception: it’s shi, not si.

su.text: Someone swinging on a rope swing with a big loop – “su-wing”.

se.text: A big mouth with a vampire fang – “say what?”

so.text: A zig-zag mouth slurping soda – “so good”.

ta.text: た is a fork and a taco side by side – “ta-co”.

chi.text: A face forced into a big “cheese!” smile. Exception: it’s chi, not ti.

tsu.text: つ is the curl of a tsunami wave. Exception: it’s tsu, not tu.

te.text: て is a telescope you hold up to your eye.

to.text: A toe with a nail stuck in it – ouch, “to(e)”.

na.text: A nun kneeling in front of a cross, praying for nachos – “na”.

nu.text: A bowl of soft noodles, loops everywhere – “nu”. Looks like め, but nu has an extra loop at the end.

ne.text: A cat curling its tail – cat is ねこ (neko). Compare れ and わ: ね ends in a loop.

no.text: の is a big “no” sign – or a pig’s nose saying “no”.

ha.text: は looks like a capital H next to a small a: “Ha!”

hi.text: A big grinning face with a huge nose: “hee hee”.

fu.text: Someone dancing with a hula hoop – “fu”. Exception: it’s fu (between h and f), not hu.

he.text: へ is the peak of a volcano like Mount St. Helens – “he”.

ho.text: A chimney next to Santa squeezing down it – “ho ho ho”.

ma.text: Mama doing magic: no head, double arms – “ma”.

mi.text: み looks like the number 21 – it’s my (“me”) lucky number.

mu.text: A cow standing in the shape of む, saying “moooo”.

me.text: め is a beautiful eye. Eye in Japanese is 目 – “me”! Like ぬ but without the extra loop.

mo.text: A fishhook with worms on it – catch “more” fish.

ya.text: A yacht with its mast and anchor – “ya”.

yu.text: A strange fish with a big eye – a “yu”-nique fish.

yo.text: A yo-yo hanging from a string – “yo”.

ra.text: A rabbit standing up, facing left with droopy ears – “ra”. The Japanese r is a light tap, between r, l and d.

ri.text: Two reeds swaying in the wind – “ri”.

ru.text: A winding route that ends in a loop – “ru”. ろ has no loop.

re.text: Someone kneeling on the ground, retching – “re”.

ro.text: A winding road with no loop at the end – “ro”. Compare る (with loop).

wa.text: A wasp with its stinger curled – “wa”.

wo.text: A creature with a hook chin going “whoa!”. Pronounced o; used almost only as the particle を.

n.text: ん looks like a handwritten lowercase n. It’s the only kana that is just a consonant.
